mergedParams.userDescription: Text animation synced to a music beat concept.

prompts.prompt: Create a dynamic text animation preset that synchronizes individual words or phrases to musical beats, where text elements cascade in with a punchy, percussive animation style. Think of this like cutting text on the beat in a music video - each word should 'hit' on a beat with impact. The text should bounce in from below with a slight overshoot, then settle into place with a subtle elastic ease. As new text enters, previous text should scale down slightly and fade to 70% opacity, creating a layered depth effect. Use the audio analysis API to detect beats and time each word's entrance accordingly. The overall composition should feel like a rhythmic typography performance where text dances to the music.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Use a BaseLayout container with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' classes. Inside, create multiple BaseLayout children with 'absolute' positioning, each containing a TextAtom. Use the audio analysis fetcher to get beat timestamps, then map each beat to a text element with relative timing. Apply a custom effect array with translateY (100% to 0%), scale (0.8 to 1.1 to 1.0), and opacity (0 to 1) keyframes. Use 'cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55)' for the elastic overshoot. Previous text elements should animate to scale(0.95) and opacity(0.7) when new text enters. Position text with 'bottom-1/3 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2' for center-bottom alignment. Set will-change: transform, opacity on animated elements. Use fitDurationTo: 'children' to match the audio duration. Consider using waveform effects with mode 'zoom' for subtle beat-reactive scaling on the active word.

prompts.prompt: Design a kinetic typography preset where text pulses and glows in sync with the bass frequencies of the music. Imagine a club VJ visualization where words throb with the beat - the text should have a neon-like glow effect that intensifies with bass hits, while the characters themselves scale rhythmically. Each word should fade in smoothly, then pulse continuously based on audio intensity. The glow should use multiple text-shadow layers that expand and contract based on frequency data. Think of this as typography that breathes with the music, where the visual energy matches the audio energy in real-time.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create a BaseLayout with 'flex items-center justify-center w-full h-full bg-black' as the container. Use TextAtom components with initial text-shadow for the glow effect. Implement waveform effects targeting 'bass' frequency with properties for scale (1.0 to 1.2), textShadow (expanding blur radius from 10px to 30px), and brightness (1.0 to 1.5). Set sensitivity to 0.8 and threshold to 0.3 for responsive but not overly sensitive reactions. Use multiple text-shadow layers in the style: '0 0 10px color, 0 0 20px color, 0 0 30px color' where color uses the audio intensity to modulate opacity. Apply 'font-bold text-6xl text-white' classes. Add a subtle continuous rotation effect with a slow ease-in-out over the full duration. Use internal effect presets like 'glow-pulse' as a base, then enhance with audio-reactive properties.

prompts.prompt: Build a split-flap display style text animation that changes words on musical beats, mimicking vintage train station or airport departure boards. Each beat should trigger a mechanical flip animation where the current text rotates out (3D rotation on X-axis) while new text rotates in. Add subtle shake effects on impact to simulate mechanical movement. The animation should feel physical and tactile, with each flip having weight and momentum. Include a brief 'blur' during the flip to simulate motion blur, and add subtle shadows to enhance the 3D effect.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'perspective-1000' class for 3D perspective. Create a flip container with 'relative preserve-3d' styles. Use two TextAtom components positioned absolutely with 'backface-hidden' - one for current text (rotateX(0deg)) and one for next text (rotateX(180deg)). On beat detection via audio analysis, trigger a rotation animation: current text animates rotateX from 0 to -180deg, next text from 180deg to 0deg. Apply 'transition-transform duration-300 ease-in-out' with transform-style: preserve-3d. Add a subtle shake effect using translateX/Y with small random values (±2px) for 50ms after each flip. Include motion blur using filter: blur(2px) at the midpoint of rotation. Use 'bg-gray-900 text-yellow-400 font-mono text-5xl px-4 py-2 rounded' for that mechanical display aesthetic. Shadow with 'drop-shadow-lg' class.

prompts.prompt: Create a particle-based text animation where letters explode and reassemble on beat drops. Think of this as a text effect you'd see in an EDM music video - letters fragment into particles that scatter outward on intense beats, then magnetically pull back together to form new words. Each particle should have its own physics-based trajectory with gravity and momentum. The explosion intensity should correlate with the beat's intensity value from audio analysis. Add light trails or motion blur to particles for a dynamic, energetic feel.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full' as container. For each word, create a wrapper BaseLayout with multiple TextAtom children (one per letter). On beat detection with high intensity (>0.7), trigger particle explosion: each letter gets random translateX(-200px to 200px), translateY(-300px to -100px), rotate(random -180 to 180deg), with initial velocity then gravity-based arc using cubic-bezier easing. Reassemble animation uses spring easing 'cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55)' to snap letters back. Apply 'absolute' positioning to each letter with calculated left positions. Add opacity fade (1 to 0.6 to 1) during explosion. Use filter effects for motion blur: 'blur(0px) to blur(3px) to blur(0px)'. Consider using internal effects with AnimationRange arrays for precise keyframe control. Set pointer-events: none during animation. Use 'text-white font-bold text-4xl' for base styling.

prompts.prompt: Design a wave-form text animation where words ripple across the screen like audio waveforms. Each word should oscillate vertically based on the audio's frequency spectrum, creating a visual equalizer effect with typography. The baseline of the text follows a sine wave pattern that modulates based on audio intensity. Higher frequencies make the text vibrate faster, lower frequencies create slower, larger waves. Think of text floating on audio waves, where each word is a boat rising and falling with the musical current.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create a BaseLayout with 'flex flex-row items-center justify-center w-full h-full gap-4'. Map each word to a TextAtom wrapped in BaseLayout with 'relative' positioning. Use waveform effects with mode: 'translate' targeting translateY. Set different frequency targets for each word position (bass for first words, mid for middle, treble for last). Apply continuous sine wave animation using custom effects: translateY with Math.sin based calculations, where amplitude is modulated by audio intensity (base ±20px, up to ±60px on peaks). Phase offset each word by index * 0.2 for wave propagation effect. Use 'inline-block' for each word container. Apply subtle rotation (-5deg to 5deg) synchronized with vertical movement. Consider using requestAnimationFrame for smooth 60fps animation if implementing custom JavaScript. Fallback to CSS keyframes with multiple percentage stops for wave motion.

prompts.prompt: Build a strobe-light text preset where words flash in and out of visibility synchronized with rapid beats or hi-hats. Similar to a club strobe effect, text should appear and disappear in sharp, staccato bursts. On strong beats, text should flash bright white with increased scale, on weaker beats it should pulse with lower intensity. Add chromatic aberration (RGB channel splitting) during intense moments for a glitchy, high-energy feel. The effect should feel aggressive and energetic, perfect for electronic or hip-hop music.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'bg-black w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center'. Create TextAtom with base opacity 0. Use audio analysis to detect beats, especially hi-hat patterns (high frequency, low intensity beats). On beat detection, flash opacity from 0 to 1 to 0 over 100ms with 'step-end' easing for sharp cuts. On strong beats (intensity > 0.8), also apply scale(1.2) and brightness(2). For chromatic aberration, use three TextAtom layers with 'absolute' positioning, slight translateX offsets (-2px, 0, 2px), and CSS mix-blend-mode: screen with red, green, blue color filters. Apply 'text-8xl font-black uppercase' for impact. Use will-change: opacity, transform, filter for performance. Consider using CSS animation with steps() timing function for true strobe effect. Add subtle background glow using box-shadow during flashes.

prompts.prompt: Create a typewriter-meets-DJ-scratch effect where text appears character by character on beats, but with a vinyl record scratch aesthetic. Each character should slide in from the side with a brief reverse motion (like a record being scratched back), then snap forward into place. Include subtle distortion or skew during the scratch motion. The typing speed should match the tempo, with faster beats creating rapid-fire typing. Add a cursor that blinks in rhythm with the music.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'font-mono text-green-400 bg-gray-900 p-8'. Use caption data to access individual characters with word-level timing. Create TextAtom for each character with initial translateX(-20px) and opacity: 0. On each beat, animate next character: translateX from -20px to 10px (reverse scratch) to 0px (settle), with skewX from 0deg to -15deg to 0deg. Duration: 200ms with 'cubic-bezier(0.11, 0, 0.5, 0)' easing. Add subtle filter: blur during motion (0 to 1px to 0). Create a cursor using ShapeAtom or '|' character that toggles opacity on beat (consider 8th note subdivision for faster blinking). Use 'inline-block' for each character to maintain spacing. Apply 'whitespace-pre' to preserve spacing. Consider adding subtle RGB noise filter during scratch for analog feel.

prompts.prompt: Design a 3D carousel text animation where words rotate around a cylinder in sync with music beats. Each beat advances the carousel by one position, bringing new text to the front while previous text rotates to the back. Think of a rotating drum or slot machine that spins to the rhythm. Text at the front should be fully visible and scaled larger, while text on the sides fades and scales down with perspective. Add momentum-based physics where faster beat sequences create faster spins with inertia.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create BaseLayout with 'perspective-1000 w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center'. Build carousel container with 'relative preserve-3d' and width/height defined. Position TextAtom elements using calculated rotateY angles (360 / wordCount * index) and translateZ for cylinder radius (e.g., 200px). On beat, rotate entire carousel container by (360 / wordCount)deg. Use 'transition-transform duration-500ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)'. Apply opacity based on rotation: front = 1, sides = 0.5, back = 0.2. Scale front text to 1.2, sides to 0.9. For momentum, track beat frequency and adjust rotation duration (faster beats = shorter duration, min 200ms). Add subtle rotateX tilt (±5deg) based on rotation direction for dynamic feel. Use 'absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2' for centering each text element.

prompts.prompt: Build a liquid text morph effect where words melt and reform on beat drops, like text made of viscous liquid responding to bass vibrations. Letters should stretch, wobble, and deform based on audio intensity, with higher intensity creating more dramatic liquification. Think of text as mercury or gel that reshapes itself to the music. Include drip effects where parts of letters occasionally drip down before snapping back. The animation should feel organic and fluid, not mechanical.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with SVG filters for liquid effects. Create TextAtom with base text, then apply SVG filter with feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap. Animate turbulence baseFrequency based on audio intensity (0.01 to 0.05). Use waveform effects targeting custom CSS variables that control filter parameters. For wobble, apply alternating scaleX (0.95 to 1.05) and scaleY (1.05 to 0.95) with sine wave patterns. Create drip effect using clip-path with animated polygon points, or use multiple TextAtom layers with different vertical positions and opacity masks. Apply 'font-black text-8xl' with text-fill-color and text-stroke for outlined liquid look. Use CSS custom properties for dynamic filter values: --turbulence, --displacement. Consider using GSAP-like morphSVG approach with path animations for true liquid morphing. Add subtle hue-rotate filter that shifts with frequency data for color-reactive liquid.

prompts.prompt: Create a glitch-hop text animation where words corrupt and reassemble on beats, inspired by digital glitches and data corruption. Text should break into horizontal slices that shift position, change colors (RGB channel separation), and distort on beat hits. Include digital artifacts like pixelation, scan lines, and data corruption characters. The glitch intensity should scale with beat intensity - subtle glitches on weak beats, complete digital chaos on drops. Think of text being processed through a broken video codec that pulses with the music.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout container using 'relative overflow-hidden bg-black'. Create multiple TextAtom layers (at least 3 for RGB channels) with 'absolute inset-0'. On beat, trigger glitch sequence: slice text into horizontal segments using clip-path rectangles, apply random translateX (±10-50px based on intensity) to each slice. Use mix-blend-mode: screen with red, green, blue colors for channel separation. Add scan lines using linear-gradient background animated with translateY. For corruption, randomly replace characters with glitch chars (▓░▒) using conditional rendering based on beat intensity. Apply CSS filters: contrast(2) brightness(1.5) during glitches. Use transform: scale3d(1, 1.02, 1) for vertical stretch distortion. Add noise using CSS paint API or SVG filters. Implement flickering with rapid opacity changes (array of 1,0,1,0,1 over 100ms). Use 'font-mono uppercase tracking-wider' for digital aesthetic. Consider data attributes for glitch text alternatives.
